utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I was informed that the parties have no preliminaries. I have one; but, meanwhile, the witness can be escorted into the courtroom. I'd like to give the guidance of the Chamber on timing of sending lists of documents to be used with witnesses. On August the 23rd, the Defence expressed concern about late notice of certain documents used by the Prosecution with Witness Doyle. The Defence then sought guidance from the Chamber about when such lists should be sent. The Chamber will not set any strict time-limits in this respect at this stage and is confident that the parties can find common ground on this issue without involving the Chamber. At the same time, the parties are encouraged to send lists of documents to be used during examination-in-chief as early as possible. The Chamber would expect that a first list of documents be sent no later than seven days prior to the witness's testimony. Such a list could then be complemented at a later stage following any proofing of the witness. And that is the guidance of the Chamber. Ms. Bibles, could you tell us how much time you would still need?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I anticipate about 20 additional minutes with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Begic. I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. That is that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. You will now be further examined by Ms. Bibles. You may proceed, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Begic.

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: When we broke yesterday, you were describing being on Vrhpolje bridge and believing that -- and I believe the quote was: "We'd been abandoned to our fate." I'd like to ask you about the circumstances at the bridge at that point in time on the 31st of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, could P163 please be brought back to our screens.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: First, could you tell us how far it is from the bridge to the water?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the bring is about 5 or 6 or perhaps 7 metres high.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And as we look at P163 on our screens, we see a number of buildings that are in the area around the bridge. What was happening with those buildings at that point in time, on 31st of May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On that day, we passed by the buildings you can see on the screen. When we arrived at the bridge, we were facing them, so you could see all of the surroundings of the village of Hrustovo and part of Vrhpolje, and everything there was on fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Was there a check-point near the bridge?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was one at the bridge itself. When you cross over the bridge and go a little further, at the cross-roads where you can take the direction for Ilidza, there was a sort of bunker where they carried out controls.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Could you tell us, looking at this photograph, whether that check-point would have on the left side or the right side of the bridge?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the right-hand side of the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: While you were at the bridge, as you described when we finished yesterday, was anything going on around that check-point?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We just saw a lot of soldiers standing on the bridge there, and there were some soldiers standing by this check-point at the cross-roads where the road leads to Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: What were these soldiers doing as the beatings were going on?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was a group standing by the railings itself on the left-hand side, on the downstream side. They were standing there and they had their rifles in their hands, and some of the soldiers were walking around the middle of the bridge. They were beating those who were standing on the other side. They were cursing. They were walking around. They were beating people, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Was anyone in your group resisting or fighting back?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not physically. But Hakija Begic, for example, said a few words quite loudly, and on the whole the others were mostly moaning and just looking at the ground, looking down in front of them. So there was no physical resistance, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yesterday you testified at, I believe it's 2151, lines 1 through 11, that Miralem Ceric and his son Enes were taken into the slaughter-house and that you didn't see them again. Did he have any other sons in your group?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Miralem Ceric.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes. Did he have any other sons who were still in your group at the bridge?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Miralem Ceric and his son Enes Ceric were behind us. His younger son, Midhet Ceric arrived at the bridge with us in the column. He was the first person there. If you are looking from the direction that we came from, he was standing there on the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Did you see whether anything happened to him on the bridge?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After they had spent some time beating the people and insulting them, one soldier asked loudly, Who was good at jumping into the water. And there was a soldier standing on the right-hand side by the railings there, Marinko Acimovic was his name, and he said I know that Cera knows how to jump into the water and then Nenad [as interpreted] Palija, who was standing in front of him, ordered Midhet to jump into the water. Midhet did so. He climbed over the railings on the bridge and jumped into the water on the upstream side. As Midhet was swimming downstream, the water took him downstream, I saw four soldiers who were preparing their automatic weapons and leaning over the railings, and when Midhet appeared under them, they opened bursts of fire directed at him. Several moments later, you could see his body a little further down. The water had carried him downstream. You could see that his body wasn't moving, and you could see that the water was red with his blood, the water around him.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And I just want to go back. Who ordered him to jump off the bridge?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nenad Kaurin, a soldier who was standing in the middle of the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And how old was Midhet?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at the time, I think he was about 30 years old.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: All right. Who was next to be ordered off the bridge?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I have said, Midhet was the first person in the column, if you are looking from -- if you are facing from the direction that we came from. And then there was Munib Begic. When Midhet was taken downstream, you could hear someone say, Let's have the next one, and then there was a soldier who had searched and beat the people earlier on. He approached. He hit him a few times with a baton. He hit him on the head a few times with a baton an ordered him to jump. He just had a look to the left, climbed over the railings, and he jumped, and a few moments later, the same thing happened. The same four men leaned over the bridge. You could hear Munib swimming and these four men firing at him.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And how old - excuse me - was Munib?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time he was 27 years old.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Who was next to go over the bridge?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next person standing by Munib was Enes Dezdarovic. He was under age at the time. He was between 15 and 16 years old. He was the next one. And to my right, two of his brothers and his father were standing to my right, in fact. He was also ordered to jump, and when this boy tried to jump into the water, and as hes with climbing over the railings, Jadranko Palija approached and shot him in the head at the time that he wanted to jump. He pushed him over the railings with his leg and when his body fell into the water and was passing under the bridge, the four men I have already mentioned fired at him again.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: At that point in time, was attention directed towards you somehow?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After they -- these people had been killed, they started beating all the others who were still standing on the bridge. Some were thrown to the ground. Some were already lying on the ground. They kicked some of them. Hit others with their rifles. It was chaos. You could no longer distinguish what was being said and to whom. There was just a lot of terrible groaning. The elderly people who were standing on the right were groaning, so this maltreatment and these beatings lasted for several minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: What was happening to you?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was also beaten, as were the others. But somehow I remained where I was standing. In other words, I wasn't lying down on the bridge. Jadranko and Nenad came and punched me in the head while I was standing there, and there was Elmedin Begic whose turn came next.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And can you describe for us what happened when it became his turn?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When it was his turn, a soldier approached and asked him who the lieutenant, the officer in Begici was, and he said, No one. He asked him who had weapons. He said he didn't know. Then they started beating the people again. They skipped him then and ordered me to open my mouth. Jadranko put the barrel of an automatic weapon in my mouth. And then someone said, Don't kill him on the bridge. Don't dirty the bridge. He should jump.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Did you, in fact, then jump?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I also climbed over the railings. I was in the middle, and then I dived into the water.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Can you describe what happened as you went into the water?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As the water was up to my neck at the place that I dived into, I hit my head because there was a rock on the bottom. I turned around and I managed to climb out under the column, the mid-column, of the bridge. I was standing there and I heard the soldiers looking for me. They were waiting to see me swimming. I knew I had to pass by. I think someone said, The water will take him away. He's certainly been stopped by this column. And then I briefly took my leave, in a certain sense. I didn't want to swim. I didn't want to be an easy target for them. I decided to swim under water. Then I took off that white T-shirt that I still had on me and kicked it to the bottom of the river, and when I had gone downstream a metre or two, I swam under water, a little to their left, and when they noticed the T-shirt, they opened bursts of fire. While I was swimming under water, I could see this. And then, as luck would have it, I avoided all those bullets. I swam under water to the left because I wanted to reach the bank, and I managed to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: How far down-river did you make it?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know exactly. Between 50 and 60 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Could you tell us, when you came up from your dive, where -- where in the stream of the river were you?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There are a lot of trees to the left of the river. A lot of bushes. There was one that was just a bit above the water. I managed to emerge by that bush, and as I emerged, I took care not to be seen. So only part of my head was above the surface of the water. I grabbed onto the bush, and that's where I remained, in hiding.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: How long did you stay in that location hidden by the bush?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I jumped off the bridge, I don't know what time it was exactly, about 5.00 or half past 5.00. I remained by the bush, observing what was going on on the bridge, and when everything was over, my intention was to get out of the river because the water was cold. However, I couldn't do so because there was still a lot of soldiers moving around by the river and in the surroundings, so I remained there. I waited for night to fall so that I would take advantage of the dark. So it was already a little dark when my intention was to get out of the water.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Let's go back to when you first came up in the bush. Could you see or hear what was going on on the bridge?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You could see everything that was going on. But from that distance and through the branches, it was difficult to see everything. You could see people jumping off the bridge. You could see the bodies falling into the water, but it wasn't possible to identify the person who had jumped into the water. You could see the same four men who continued to fire. You could hear people groaning and moaning. They continued with their beatings. There was a lot of noise they were making. They continued cursing.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Were you able -- are you able to tell us how many bodies went off the bridge after you surfaced at the bush?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw two or three other bodies that jumped off the bridge, or were thrown off the bridge, after I had jumped. Not everyone jumped off the bridge. After the two or three bodies that jumped, the two or three people that jumped into the water, you could hear them opening bursts of fire for quite some time, and then there was silence for a while. You could no longer hear anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: At some point, did you attempt to find other survivors from the bridge?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I managed to get out of the water, over the next few days, I spent some time walking around the area in an attempt to see if I could find anyone, but I didn't find anyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My I just interrupt, Madam Bibles. At page 9, line 13, the witness says or is interpreted to have said: "After the two or three bodies that jumped, the two or three people that jumped into the water, you could hear them opening bursts of fire for quite some time and then there was silence for a while." Did you mean to say that the people who are jumping into the water fired shots? Or were they fired at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. What I said was that from where I was in the water, I could observe the same scenario repeating itself a few times. The man would jump. Then the four would fire. After that, would you hear a long burst of fire. After the scenario repeated itself three times, then you would hear the long burst of fire. And then after that shooting, no more people jumped in the water and you couldn't hear any more moaning or cursing. It's as if there is nobody there on the bridge anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: What sort of injuries did you have in the -- after the -- the bridge?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was beaten on the bridge. I had some bruises around my eyes. When I jumped into the water, when I dived, I hurt my head. My skull cracked open in one place, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: You testified that over the next few days you spent some time walking around the area. What area did you stay near during those few days?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After it got dark, then I was thinking that I should get out of the river, but I had already bled a lot and I was cold. So the water just carried me downstream. And then the next day, or a couple of days later, I woke up at the delta of the Sanica river, and I was there by a bridge, and I spent the next couple of days there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: At some point, did you decide that you needed to go for help?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I spent three nights there where the Sana and the Sanica rivers meet, and then when I could no longer stand being there, I decided to leave and go somewhere. I decided to go to Andja Krlic and Vid Krlic. And so that one night when there was a storm, I took the opportunity and I went to their house, and I asked them for help.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And just to clarify, was this your godmother?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Did you actually -- were you able to reach her?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, yes. Like I said, that night, when I decided to go somewhere else, it was a terrible storm. It was raining. There was thunder and lightening, so I used that very dark time to reach their house, unnoticed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: When you reached her, did she tend to your wounds?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I arrived after midnight. And in the state that I was in, I didn't dare to knock on the door. I hid in the barn. And only when it was light, when they came out of their house, then I said something. They received me. They told me that they knew what had happened. They brought me into the house, and then my godmother Andja brought some plum brandy to clean my wound on my head. She cleaned the area around my eyes, and then she put some kind of dressing on my chest. I put some dry clothing on, and I had a cup of tea.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: You told us that her family -- this was a Serb family. Did they have Serb neighbours who were concerned for their own safety because you were with them?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Her son Zeljko was also an armed soldier. At that time he just happened to be at home. The check-point that was not far from our houses was a joint check-point for the Serbian population in the surrounding houses. From Vehici [phoen] to my godmother Andja's house, there was no check-point. At least I didn't see any. There was just one check-point more to the right, near the Stojnovics' place.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Did someone turn you in to the authorities?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After 15 or 20 minutes, I was so tired. At one point, I woke up. There was nobody in the room, and you could hear voices calling me to come outside. I went outside, and then I could see neighbours who had surrounded the house. They were armed and they were telling me to surrender.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And did you, in fact, surrender?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I went out. I knew my neighbours. There was an officer with them. My godmother Andja and her son were standing there with them when I came out. Then the people who had surrounded the house also came, so we were all standing together in one place near the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: All right. After you surrendered, did you receive medical care?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At that point, no. This officer was in two minds, the one who came with the car and the neighbours. His only dilemma was what was I doing there. Who was I. Why did I come there. He was asking Andja. Actually, she explained to him that I was her godchild and that I could stay at their place, which is what he was asking. He asked, Can he stay with you for a couple of days until the situation calms down a little bit? She said, Yes, he can. But the neighbours who were with this officer were not in favour of my staying. They wanted him to drive me away from that place because I posed a danger for them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: All right. Going forward in time, at some point in time, did you end up going to Manjaca camp?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In July, when the inmates were taken to Manjaca that day, I was also in one of those trucks.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Where were you immediately before being taken to Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I was taken from my godmother Andja's house, they took me to the village of Tomina. That's where I received medical treatment. They interrogated me, and after this interrogation, I was released. Actually, I was taken to the village of Tomina which was across the river from our village, and that's where the refugees were located, from Begici. My mother was there and my youngest brother. We were some 20 days there. And then, after that, all the refugees from the neighbouring villages were transferred to the Krings camp in Sanski Most. And then after a couple of days, or three days, we were transferred to Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: How long were you in Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there until the 16th of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And from there, you were eventually released?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When the camp was disbanded, I was released with the other inmates. We went to the town of Karlovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Did your mother and youngest brother survive the war?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were transported from the Krings camp before I was. They were taken to Central Bosnia. And then I think they went to Slovenia. Through the Red Cross, I think it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Are you aware of whether or not an exhumation was done of bodies under the Vrhpolje?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is interest any dispute about these matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, why then ask the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Especially if you indicate that you need another 20 minutes. You've taken now approximately 30, and then to come up with matters which are not in dispute, and I take it that there is documentary evidence of it anyhow.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I won't be asking more than one question with respect to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Do you know whether the remains of any of your immediate family was identified in the exhumation?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many of them were found. Among them, my brother, Nedzad Begic, my younger brother.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I am coming to the end, I would ask that 65 ter 28366 be brought to our screens.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: While that's being brought up, have you looked at a list of names, the list of names you see before you, before testifying?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And the list of names, can you tell us just briefly who these people are. How is it that -- that their names are all together?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a list of the people who went to that bridge that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Have you seen or heard of any of the people whose names are on this list? Have you heard of any of them being alive since the 31st of May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution tendered 65 ter 28366 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's not clear who created this document, and we would object to this kind of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First question: Who created it?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, this was created from the witness's statement by the Office of the Prosecutor and then shown to the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: -- over the weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is extracted from previous statements and testimony, is that?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And also we would ask where in the indictment we have those names or this list?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, this would be for Scheduled Incident A71.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, this refers to, as I said, Scheduled Incident A71. There was a separate list filed with the names of the victims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We -- as we stated before, we would -- we would always object to the documents created in this way by the Office of the Prosecutor. It's up to Your Honours to decide what to do with this kind of document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What basis? I mean, of course, what we could do now, the witness recognises, as he has testified, that these are names of persons he knows were in the -- taken to the bridge. Now, of course, we could ask him to -- or to put on the record each individual name and ask him to confirm that this was a person. That seems not to be very practical. It's not clear to me on what basis you exactly oppose the admission of the list, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's more --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What legal basis, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Legal basis: That it's more of a -- actually -- just a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it is different from the one -- from the indictment, so why don't they show the witness that list? We would object because it was created by the Office of the Prosecutor. It's -- it's, I think, not good to let parties to create documents and ask for their admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A lot of photographs, for example, are produced by the Office of the Prosecution as well. I mean, I never heard that that makes them in any way inadmissible. Now, often we see that. But I'll consult with my colleagues about admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have a few questions for the witness. Witness, I'll read the names, and you confirm by a yes or a no whether they were in the group that were led to the bridge. Elmedin Begic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
