utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No further questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Not with respect to this exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, is there any need to insist on the exhibit to be admitted -- have it admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. The record is very clear at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed and keep in mind that you went well beyond your 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I apologise for that, Your Honour. We did reserve two hours for this witness and I was overambitious in my time. I have one last question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please put it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Could you describe for us the last time that you saw your brother Nedzad?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At one point when I was standing on the bridge. I was the fourth in line. My younger brother, Nedzad, was the last one in the column that was standing along the fence, and when I was jumping off the bridge, at that point I looked at him and he looked at me also. Then that was the only -- actually, that was the last time that we saw each other.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Bibles. Mr. Lukic, are you ready to cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Begic, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. And you'll find him on your left.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Begic.

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As you heard from His Honour, I'm going to be cross-examining you now on behalf of the Defence of General Mladic. Today, on page 3 of the transcript, you talked about Vrhpolje and Hrustovo.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the last part of his question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that Hrustovo and Vrhpolje were strong military points of the Muslim army?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know the brothers Vukanovic?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that they were the commanders of these military units in Hrustovo and Vrhpolje?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear about it, but I didn't know it myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And are you aware that, at the time, there were 900 members of the Bosnia-Herzegovina TO in Vrhpolje at the time?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And are you aware that in Mahala and Hrustovo there were 400 members of the B and H TO?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that on the 26th May 1992, there was a mortar attack initiated from Mahala on the Serbian parts of Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was in Begici at the time which is 10 kilometres away, so I didn't see or hear anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the time that you're speaking of, did you know that the fighting in Vrhpolje precisely on that day resulted in the death of ten members of the Serbian army in combat?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that on that day 146 fighters of the TO of the Bosnia-Herzegovina forces surrendered in the fighting in Vrhpolje?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm hearing of that for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And have you ever had heard of Amir Avdic, who was one of the commanders of those forces?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And did you know that he was one of the commanders of those forces?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At that point, no, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And did you hear about that later?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please look at P163 on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you were describing how people slipped through the gaps in the fence of the bridge or the railing, is this how this railing looked at the time?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And how high is it?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1 metre. I don't know exactly. Approximately 1 metre.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And how is it possible for a person to slip through this railing?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through the top. Because the railing only has one bar going through the middle. And then they would slip through this upper part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't understand you. They passed through what?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through the railing. This is a picture of the bridge after it was repaired, after the war. It's an identical -- the railing is identical, but you could slip through this top frame of the railing. You could slip through it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you saying that the people were sliding through between the asphalt and that wrung, that railing?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you put to the witness that he used the words "slip through." Could you give us the exact line where he said so, so that we are able to follow your examination. Because a WordWheel search on the yesterday and today, only gives one -- let me see ... I only see the word -- oh, let me see. I didn't find it. Could you assist me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm trying, Your Honour. For example, today, on page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see. Page 4, you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have line 3. But let me look ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 4, line 3 of today's transcript, I do not find anything of the kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After that. I don't have the exact page and line. He was talking about Midhet. Here it was marked: He climbed over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He climbed over. That's not the same as slipping through, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But in his statement, I found that he said "through."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This statement is not in evidence, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It will be. It will be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I do understand that you want to tender it soon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, I will tender it soon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll wait and see. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: At page 21, line -- line 22, the witness says, after being asked a question: "I'm sorry, I didn't understand you. They passed through what?" The answer was: "Through the railing."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is a picture of the bridge after it was repaired after the war. It's an identical -- the railing is identical, but you could slip through this top frame of the railing. You could slip through it. The point I want to raise with you is that he could slip through that top. Now, at page 22, you -- line 1, you say: "Are you saying that the people were sliding through between the asphalt and that wrung, that railing?"

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, if they were slipping through the top as he has already told you, it couldn't be between the asphalt and the railing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But then he confirmed what I asked him, because there was no possibility to -- there is only one gap in between the railing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's not further --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's not further discuss it at this moment, but there certainly is some confusion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're confusing the witness. This is the point. Because he has given you an answer and you ask the same question again and ask it differently. He said they go over the top. Now you say it's between the asphalt and the wrungs. Obviously if it is between the asphalt and the wrungs, it means they are sliding on [indiscernible] virtually, when in fact he says they are climbing on the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There was nothing on the top to squeeze through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, on the top he said this railing has a bar in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So you jump over.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- only one bar. Only one bar. There is nothing to be squeezed through on the top.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if it confuses us, it most likely would have confused the witness as well, whatever he answered. And if you say he confirmed that, it could be because he was confused. That, at least, is a possibility which we should exclude for your next questions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll go on, Mr. Begic. We'll get to that. I'll find it in your statement as well. You saw bodies floating downstream. You saw that from the bridge; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. From the bridge, you could hear someone below the bridge, but you couldn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. But when people were hit, did you see --

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And how far away would they float when you could see them?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, after 30 or 40 metres, you could already see the water and a body floating on the water.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then, when you grabbed onto a piece of wood when you first got out --

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- all these bodies -- all the bodies of the persons before you, did they already go downstream?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where they ended up, because we could see them floating down the river from the bridge, but not all the time because we were being beaten and everything else. So our attention was diverted and we could not watch these bodies for a very long time as they went downstream. I mean, you couldn't watch downstream any longer and you couldn't see where they ended up.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now take a look of the statement of the witness from the 16th of April, 1996; 1D205.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the statement that you gave on the 16th of April, 1996 at the court in Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the bottom of the page, is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please take a look at page 7 now in both languages, B/C/S and English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since this statement is rather condensed, there are no paragraphs so we'll have to count the lines. Today, you said that you got out of the water after 50 or 60 metres --

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And in line five in B/C/S and in line 24 on the same page in English, you say that you dived and swam under water for about 100 to 150 metres. Can you reconcile the two statements for us today? Can you tell us what is correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To this day, I cannot say exactly how far away it was from the bridge to that bush. Now, when I think of it, it seems to be about 150 metres. Sometimes I say 50. But, at any rate, the distance was at least 50 and then up to 150 metres. That would be the most accurate way of putting it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At any rate, you said in your statement that you no longer saw the bodies of the persons who got into the water before you, and you confirmed that for us today.

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So they floated down these 50 or 150 metres. They floated downstream?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And where is the grave where they were found later on? That is unclear to me. Is it the grave below that bridge from which the people allegedly jumped or is it a different bridge?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there are several graves. And the bodies of the persons who were on the bridge were identified. Some were found in the grave under the bridge and others at other locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would need guidance from Your Honours. Are we going to have short sittings today and short breaks?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we have -- I -- I should have been more alert on the short sessions. If this would be a suitable moment for you to take a break?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take the break now and then resume at ten minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we take short breaks then. I'm confusing you at this very moment as well. Apologies for that. Could the witness first be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will resume, after a short break, at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. Lukic, the Chamber was also a bit puzzled by the reference to "grave." I think the witness said something about an exhumation. Grave, exhumation, I do not know whether it was a primary or secondary grave, et cetera. But, certainly, the witness did not use the word "grave," but it may be in the statement. But, again, the statement is not in evidence and the Chamber has not read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Welcome back, Mr. Begic. Mr. Lukic will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Begic, just briefly I will go back to the bridge railing. We already have your statement on our screens, but we need page 5 in B/C/S and page 6 in English. First of all, I would like to show the Judges that there was no ill-intent on my part when I referred to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the B/C/S version, we need line 12 from the bottom up. In the English version, we need line 4 on page 6. Line 4 from the top. Everyone can see it in the English version now. This is what is written: "He squeezed through the fence and jumped into the water head first." The same is written in the B/C/S version. I'm going to read B/C/S now. "He squeezed through the fence and then jumped into the water head first." [In English] This is just for the clarification that I really found it in the -- in the -- in his statement, and I wasn't misleading this witness, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's not discuss this any further. What you appropriately should have done is to put this to the witness because at -- certainly you confused the Chamber if you are referring to portions of a statement which the Chamber is unaware of and then ask questions about it. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But also jumping through the fence. You can jump -- jumping through the fence is more in line with jumping over -- over the top rather than sliding underneath.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was clear, Your Honour. Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're not going to deal with this any longer, Mr. Begic. I'm going to move onto something completely different now, when you say that local Serbs from the village of Cosici and Stojinovici placed a check-point 800 metres from your village.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have page 2, lines 4 through 6 in B/C/S, and page 2, lines 7 through 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You speak about a commander here who brought the unit to your village on the 25th of May, and this is what you say. You see line 3: "That unit which come to our village on the 25th of May, 1992, was commanded by a commander with long black hair, tied in a ponytail. He wore round dark glasses." And then further on you say: "He wore black leather gloves which he never took off." Would you say the same thing today if you were to describe this commander?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Also, on the same page of the B/C/S version but line 6 from the bottom up; and, in English, it is page 3, line 2 from the top. You describe the 31st of May, 1992, so this is the day when these killings happened, as you had said. And again you describe this commander, and you say: "The unit was commanded by the Chetnik whom I previously described as having a long ponytail." Would you say the same thing today as well?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to ask you something. Since we are describing the check-point in Cosici and Stojinovici now, is it correct that Muslims had a check-point as well but in the village of Crnojevici at the time?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where that village is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Crnojevic. Perhaps it was mistaken there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D207, could we please see that in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Begic, I'll read through it so that it can be correctly interpreted. This is a transcript from the Brdjanin case. Page 6382. The date of the trial was the 31st of May, 2001, when you testified in that case, and Ms. Faveau-Ivanovic, or Mrs. Faveau-Ivanovic, asked you the following: [In English] "Is it not true that Muslims also set up check-points in their villages and hamlets?" [Interpretation] And your answer at point 17 is: "It is true, they set up a check-point at the village of Crnojevici?" It hasn't been correctly noted here. What did you have in mind? Where did the Muslims set up a check-point at the time?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember this statement, a check-point in Crnojevici.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we go to the top of the page, please. Could you zoom in to the top left-hand corner so that the witness can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says the witness is Rajif Begic and that he was testifying in open session. Do you remember testifying in the Brdjanin case?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You don't know what you were testifying about exactly at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was probably thinking about a station, a Vrhpolje station, but I didn't see any large check-points in the hamlets, so I couldn't really say that there was a check-point there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you're telling us that on the 31st of May, 2002, in fact, you weren't telling us the truth?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not familiar with the existence of a village called Crnojevici. I don't know how it is that this name, Crnojevici, appears in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. We will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the language on the 31st of May is not unambiguous, and I think it would be fair to -- to the witness to acknowledge that. The question was: "You said yesterday that your Serb neighbours set up check-points. Is it not true that Muslim also set up check-points in their villages and hamlets?" When the witness said it is true that they set up a check-point at the village of Crnojevici, then it's unclear who are the "they," because in the question setting up check-points is referred to both by Serbs and by Muslims so --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the "they" is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The question was Muslims, specific. Is it not true that Muslims also set up check-points. It is it true --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was introduced by: "You said yesterday that your Serb neighbours set up check-points."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "Is it also not true that Muslims also set up check-points?"

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If a witness then answers: "It is true that they set up check-points," there may be ambiguity as whether the witness responds to the introduction to the question or the question itself. That is ambiguous. I do not need any further discussion at this moment about it, but I would like to have it put on the record. You may proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, in this transcript he wasn't answering to my question. He was -- in this transcript he was answering to question of my colleague Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I said that from reading it that it seems, at least, ambiguous. Not to say that you're right or wrong, but at least there's some ambiguity in the day and that's what I wanted to put on the record, and you may now proceed. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I can inquire that "they" is ambiguous in today's transcript or in the transcript from the 31st of May, 2002?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 31st of May, Mr. Lukic. And, as I said before, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the same statement on the second page --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We no longer need the transcript. We need this witness's statement, 1D205. Page 2 in both versions. It's the 14th line from the bottom in the B/C/S version; and it's the sixth line from the bottom in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Begic, here, you say: "The entire municipality was attacked. The town of Sanski Most itself and the villages of Hrustovo and Vrhpolje. It was relatively calm in our village up until the 31st of May, 1992." When the attack was carried out against the villages of Hrustovo and Vrhpolje, do you know how long it lasted?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether any resistance was mounted?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now very briefly, I'd like to deal with the part of your testimony when you say that Nedjo Sucur [phoen] interrogated you in the school.

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He asked you whether you knew Nenad Kaurin; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Nenad, according to you, was one of the people who opened fire on the bridge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that you knew him and that he was a member of the reserve police force; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He also wore a blue police uniform and a blue cap.

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, could we have a look at Exhibit P162.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have that up on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Begic, this is an exhibit that we have already had a look at. It's a drawing of the Sanski Most municipality and the villages have been marked. We can see it now. Could we have one map shown on the entire screen. It would be easier?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: English or B/C/S version, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: B/C/S version so that the witness can see it more properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With regard to this document I'd like to ask you the following. At the top, we can see various colours that reflect the ethnic composition of that municipality. Did you make this sketch?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did I draw this map? No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you work out the ethnic composition of the population. It says in 1991 the ethnic composition was such and such, and in 1995 it was such and such.

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps, but I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you draw this map?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Here the ethnic composition of the population as represented in 1991 and in 1995. You have the English version of the map in front of you. Perhaps that is causing some confusion but it doesn't matter. I had a look at the map and calculated that there were 19 Serbian villages depicted on the map. Can you tell us what the ethnic composition of the Sanski Most municipality is today? What is the percentage of Serbs living in the municipality of Sanski Most today? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So could we agree that there are very few Serbs in the municipality now?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we could agree on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now go back to your statement, 1D205. Page 5, line 12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you didn't object to the admission of P162. Nevertheless, of course, it raises some questions. Ms. Bibles, you used this map, and -- which depicts apparently the ethnic composition of the various villages. The only thing you asked the witness about was whether it's in the southeastern area, that's where he lived, and you mentioned a few -- was it your intention to establish in any way the ethnic composition, either in 1992 or at 1995? Because if that's the case, you should have asked the witness questions about it. And if you did not intend to do that, why didn't you use a map without any ethnic compositions? That's -- again, Mr. Lukic, you did not object. But I think, in view of your questions, it's important for us to know what you intended to prove with this map because you didn't ask any question about what seems to be the core of this map. That is, ethnic composition.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, the intent of the question was as the witness was describing. Sanski Most in 1992 was to display Sanski Most as an area that had villages of all ethnicities, and particularly with respect to his area that they were mixed. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, first of all, you didn't ask any such question from the witness, so it is not the appropriate way of establishing that by remaining silent on it and just putting the colours on our screens. That's one. Second, if it was your intention to intention to establish the composition, the ethnic composition of the villages in 1992, or at least at the beginning of the conflict, then I think there exists a one -- 1991 census, at least not unknown in this Tribunal, which gives the details. So then it would have been appropriate, first of all, to try to agree with Mr. Lukic about the ethnic composition of villages in Sanski Most and then to present that either as an agreed fact or to do that not through a witness which remains completely silent on the matter, but then, rather, bar table the census on Sanski Most. This is not the way the Chamber expects the Prosecution to proceed in these kind of matters. Irrespective of whether Mr. Lukic objects to the admission, yes or no. May this serve you as guidance. Mr. Lukic, sorry for the interruption. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need to have a look at your statement, page 5 line 12 in the B/C/S version. It's page 5 and line 23 in the English version. Here you mention --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, we still don't know where we are on the English statement. We don't see the page, we don't see the lines. We can't count line 27 because -- that's better. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it's line 23, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Here you say: "He told us to line up on the bridge in single file, half a metre apart, and take off all our clothes, except for T-shirts ..." Did you obey the person who ordered to you take everything off, apart from your T-shirts?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they order you to take your clothes off, well, that person didn't say that everyone should remain in their T-shirts. Everyone was ordered to take their clothes off. Some took everything off apart from their T-shirts. Some remained in their shirts and trousers, but the person did not say that people should remain in their T-shirts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page 76, lines 3 to 7, you yesterday said that someone remained -- some remained wearing their trousers, some wearing two T-shirts, or shirts, but no one kept their shoes on.

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So what you said in your statement can't be accepted, what you said in the transcript should be accepted?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What did I say in the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I asked you whether you obeyed this person. Did you obey him? How did you act?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we obeyed him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My colleague asked you about the injuries you sustained today [as interpreted], and you said that you -- your eye had been wounded and your head as well, because of the beating.

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You didn't have any other injuries?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had been beaten in the stomach, the ribs, but I was visibly injured in the head when I was beaten. And when I jumped into the water I hit a rock, as a result of which I had a wound to the head.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have a look at page 7, line 7 in the B/C/S version, and in the English version, let's have a look at page 7, line 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your statement, line 7, as you can see, or, rather, it starts at line 6, towards the end of line 6. It says: "While I was swimming underwater, I felt that I had been injured in the area of the left shoulder." Were you wounded in that area on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was swimming underwater by the T-shirt, a bullet whizzed by, grazed my left shoulder, so I was only grazed. I didn't bleed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you were wounded in the area of the left shoulder?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that someone designated you as a person who had weapons?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the bridge, when it was Elmedin Begic's turn, when the soldier ordering us to jump from the bridge asked him who had weapons, Elmedin pointed to the right and said, They had. But he didn't say Raho had or someone else had. He said, They had weapons, and what he had in mind were the weapons that were handed over at the check-point in Stojinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then you go on to say that you were beaten by Chetniks on the bridge. What kind of insignia did they have, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had different insignia. Like I said, some were wearing military uniforms. Some were wearing blue uniforms. Some had Chetnik insignia. Some had just regular items of clothing, waistcoats, jackets, so it was all mixed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But among the soldiers who came on the 25th of May, 1992, you didn't recognise anyone because you were hiding. But your mother recognised your school friend, Dusko Savic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before and at that time he was living in Kljevci; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The second time when they came, they beat up three men: Kurbegovic, Ismet, Hakija Begici, and Sacir Begic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time when they came on the 31st of May, they didn't beat anyone when we set off.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So this was between the 25th and the 31st. When they came that time, is it correct that these three men were beaten?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came a number of times and they beat these three men.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: According to you it was Ranko Cosic, Vico Ilic, Bosko Stojanovic who beat these men up; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And did they also live in the neighbouring villages of Cosici and Stojinovici?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you saw these same people on the 31st of May 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They didn't come that day when they were taking us away.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Also in the Brdjanin case - we don't need to call up the document, it's page 6389 in e-court - you said that they wore different things on their heads, some of them had helmets and others were wearing different caps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And in response to a request by my colleague Ms. Fauveau, so in Brdjanin on the 30th of May, page 8689, when asked, you said that all men wore some kind of uniform - is that correct? - and you answered in the affirmative. You said yes. Would you still stand by that statement?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not get the transcript page and line numbers for the previous question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would read the transcript, page 41, the interpreter didn't get the transcript page and line numbers for the previous question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first page was 6389 and the second page was 6389, also. I just gave the line numbers, from 17 to 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now I would like you to tell us this. In response to His Honour Judge Agius's question on page 6399, line 11, of the Brdjanin trial of the 30th of May, you said - and you gave a longer answer, I'm summarising: Members of these units were not members of the regular military force. Would you still say the same thing today?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, without knowing the context of, for example, "these men." Of course the Chamber, if it's not in evidence, has got no idea what "these men" are, what it refers to, et cetera. So if you want us to take these matters seriously you should, one way or another, either to provide that one page or -- so that we can place it in time that we can have the right reference as far as time and place is concerned. Are we still talking about the people coming to the village? Are we talking about the people taking him to the bridge? "These men" is really creating a puzzle for us rather than it gives answers. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'm going to try to correct this error right now. Can we please look at e-court 1D209, which is the page that I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can only see a part of the question by His Honour Judge Agius.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably we would need to look at the previous page, but we did not upload it. But we're going to show this exhibit -- actually, this exhibit, which we would like to tender. We have the answer of the witness. I will broaden my question so that it's clearer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And so, Mr. Begic, I'm going to ask you in order to explain things better, thus, the people who came on the 25th of May, 1992, in uniform, Serbs, with weapons, and then these same people who came, the ones in uniform, with weapons, Serbs, on the 31st of May, 1990 [as interpreted], were not members of regular army forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Begic. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could -- Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, one thing. We were -- we had the statement ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We had the statement of this gentleman, 1D205. We would like to tendered it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Without any limits, Mr. Lukic, which means that all the inculpatory elements of that statement would be in evidence as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can cut off the portions if Your Honours want us -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We do not want it. I'm just pointing at the consequences as far as the -- if you -- and, of course, there's another problem: If you want to tender this into evidence, then we are -- is this the statement taken by the local authorities?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not for the purposes of this Tribunal, which means that it does not fall within the scope of 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's true, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then I will skip -- I will withdraw our request. We don't need the statement since the gentleman answered all our questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the Chamber gained the impression that you read into the transcripts all the relevant portions of that statement. Under those circumstances, and I think that is what you hinted at, that you were considering to withdraw tendering his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that is the case, then we don't have to decide on the matter. There was another issue about the transcript. Let me see. There was something about the year, 1990. Let me see ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There was -- if you look with me at page 42, your question --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which page -- which line, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 42. It is for me line 17: "... with weapons, Serbs, on the 31st of May 1990 ..." I may take it that you intended to refer to 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 1992. And I think that I said so and the witness heard the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Then that is corrected. There seems to be little chance of real confusion there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any -- if this concludes your cross-examination, I'll just check with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber at this moment has no further questions. Ms. Bibles, is there any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Begic, then this concludes your testimony in this case. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague -- yes, Mr. Begic. You wanted to address me. Please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. If you permit me, Your Honour, I would like to say something. I would actually like to go back to Mr. Lukic's question about the bridge. It's correct that I said that those were killed squeezed through between the railings, so I don't want this to be in doubt at any point, how my friends and my neighbours were killed. I said that we squeezed through and that is correct. Even today can you still squeeze through the railing, even though it's a little bit hard to see in the photograph. But the way in which Dizdarevic, Enes was killed is exactly the way I described it, and I would like the statement to remain just as it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, which I do understand now is that he squeezed through the upper part of the railing and what a bar below that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So just under the very top but not over --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the middle, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the middle. This correction --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Begic, for that. Mr. Lukic, no further questions on that. Ms. Bibles, the same. Then thank you for this clarification. Then I, again, want to thank you - that was what I was doing - for coming to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that are put to you by the parties and by the Bench, and I wish you a safe journey back home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness is excused. He may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In a few minutes, Your Honour. Based on my earlier conversation with Mr. Lukic, he thought that he would take the entire session, so we had arranged for the witness to be brought at noon. As soon as he said he was sitting down I sent an e-mail and they are bringing the witness over now, but it may still take a few minutes for the witness to arrive. I do have a short matter that I could deal with at this time to make productive use of the time, but it will be a few minutes before the witness is in the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see that. Now usually the last part of the morning session is a bit shorter. Now we could also, after you have dealt with the matter you wanted to raise, we could also take the break then and then have two sessions of approximately equal length.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I think that would ensure that the witness is here at that stage, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The matter you would like to raise at this moment is which one, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, prior to the summer recess the Chamber had raised concerns about the fact that the Prosecution had not used consistent colours in the Sarajevo court binder to denote the locations of the VRS and ABiH front lines. We've examined the map book more closely and in fact we have used colours consistently, and we - in any map produced by the Prosecution - we've used the colour red to mark the location of ABiH forces and blue to mark the location of Bosnian Serb forces. The problem is in the VRS maps, some of which are reproduced, in those maps the colours are not used consistently. So thus in the VRS map reproduced at page 1 of the map book, the VRS used red to mark the location of the ABiH forces and blue to denote VRS forces. They used the opposite colour scheme in the VRS map reproduced at page 49. So that's an explanation of the different colours, and if the Chamber would wish us to create an explanation or insert to add to P3, which is that map book, the Prosecution would be happy to undertake that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd first like to take a look at what you just explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: They were the maps on pages 1 and 49.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm just looking at them now. I do see that opposite colours are used. I think, as a matter of fact, but I'm looking at my colleagues, that we should not in any way change any of the original maps, and I think that your explanation at this moment is clear to us and enables us to work on the basis of the material we find in that binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, should we ever use these maps with witnesses, we will remind the Chamber of the possible confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that explanation. Mr. Lukic, unless there's any matter -- and I see that Mr. Mladic apparently wants to consult with you. Perhaps you --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to say a couple of things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, you first have to consult with Mr. Lukic about what you intend to say because you're represented by him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And perhaps what we best could do is to take the break now, both for the witness to arrive and for you, Mr. Lukic, to further consult with Mr. Mladic. We take a break and we resume at ten minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, we ended the last session you consulting with Mr. Mladic. I do understand from your body language that there's nothing to be raised at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's true, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll proceed. Is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Hochhauser.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER

It's been shown to the witness outside the courtroom, and so, Your Honours, if -- if it pleases the Court, and that route is acceptable to the Court, I would ask that that proofing note be allowed to be assigned a 65 ter number and we'll show to the witness during the course of the examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm a bit confused. 65 ter numbers are not assigned but are -- by yourself, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Ah, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore there's no need --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I just meant to add it to our 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 65 ter list, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And the number would be 28371.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ivetic, no objections against adding it to the 65 ter [overlapping speakers]?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Nothing, Your Honours. It's of an accurately reflect -- the statement -- the discussions have been accurately reflected that took place during the pause.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Leave is granted to add the proofing note to the 65 ter exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I would just add to that, because this came up unexpectedly, although we had -- we had entered into e-court just the redacted version that we thought we would be showing, the entire proofing is not yet in e-court but I have hard copies to provide to the witness and to the Bench, and we hope that it will be up in e-court within the next five to ten minutes.

utterances.text: The next witness the Prosecution calls will be, Ms. Hochhauser?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Hurko --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I presume. Mr. Hurko, before you give evidence, the Rules require you to make a solemn declaration. The text is now handed out to you. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
